title: JSX, Components, and Props
description: Understand how to use JSX syntax, create functional components, and pass data using props in React Native.

lessons.title: What is JSX?
lessons.content:
JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It's a syntax extension that looks similar to HTML and is used in React to describe UI structure.

Example:
```jsx
const element = <Text>Hello, world!</Text>;
```
JSX makes it easier to write and visualize the UI layout in code.

lessons.title: Rendering Elements in JSX
Creating Functional Components
Component Hierarchy
lessons.content:
React Native apps are built using small components. Components can contain other components, creating a hierarchy or tree structure.

Example:
`App` ➝ `Header`, `MainContent`, `Footer`

lessons.title: Using Props in Components
Default Props
PropTypes for Type Checking
Props vs State
lessons.content: `Props` are read-only and passed from parent to child. `State` is local to a component and can change over time.

lessons.title: Self-closing Components and Nesting
lessons.content:
Use self-closing tags when there are no children.

```jsx
<Image source={...} />

<View>
  <Text>Nested inside a view</Text>
</View>
```

lessons.title: Best Practices for JSX and Props
lessons.content:
- Keep components small and focused.
- Use clear and descriptive prop names.
- Avoid deeply nested structures when possible.
- Comment your JSX when needed for clarity.
